title: Ergodicity
description: The double well $\Psi = \frac{(x^2 - 4)^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{2}$, all particles start in the left well. The Ergodicity window follows one particle (ringed) and plots its time average $\frac{1}{t}\int_0^t X^1_s\,ds$ against the mean of $X^1$ over all particles at the same instant. For an ergodic process both converge to $\int x\,d\pi = 0$.

questions.text: Which one gets close to 0 first: the time average of the ringed particle or the ensemble mean? Why?
What do both averages converge to in the long run?
Lower σ to 0.7 and follow another particle. What happens to its time average over the same time? What does this say about the mixing time?
Is the time average of a single run a good estimator of $\int f\,d\pi$ here? When is it, in general?
